items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: There was only one person he knew. And that was me.

ctx.x: Can you give the instruments to the people who want to know?

He played clarinet. Eddie Rowland, after two weeks, they were thrown out of a job. And he was put in jail for no visible means of support. There was only one person he knew. And that was me. Because I happened to be the oldest musician of the bunch that ever went off and played up around out of town. And I had to pay his way out of jail was $25. Put him on a train and sent him back to New Orleans. I have never received one penny from him. He's dead now up to this day. Went in a lock, split business, some way down…
What was his name again? Carter?

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: Well, I'll tell you one was Eddie Rowland. He came up there with Tom Brown's reorganized band.

ctx.x: You don't see anything in front of me that I take notes from, only just from what comes to my mind. That's why I don't have it in chronological order. I can only tell you what I can think of at the time. Maybe my talk may be gobbled up a little bit, that I might put this one before the other one, the other one before the other one. But I am telling you the true facts of this music. It was in Chicago where I changed the rhythm. They had a certain dance team. They were doing a castle walk. And up in the north,…
Can you hold it a second?
